tagline: Past a town of eighteen, up the coast to the seals.
intro: Highway 1 leaves San Luis Obispo as a four-lane road and comes back to the coast at Morro Bay, where Morro Rock stands at the harbor mouth. North of Cayucos it narrows. From there it is a winding two-lane road with an occasional passing lane, through Cambria and San Simeon and on to the Monterey County line.

The coastal hills between Cayucos and Cambria were dairy country from the 1860s, settled by Swiss and Italian immigrants. Up on the hill at San Simeon is the estate William Randolph Hearst and his architect Julia Morgan kept building from 1919 until 1947.

moments.title: Morro Rock
moments.text: A volcanic plug 581 feet high, tied to the shore by a causeway and held sacred by both the Salinan and the Chumash.

moments.title: Harmony
moments.text: An 1869 creamery town of one block whose sign long gave the population as 18. Its parade, with nowhere to go, stood still while the spectators walked around it.

moments.title: Piedras Blancas
moments.text: About a mile south of the 1875 lighthouse, a boardwalk looks over an elephant seal rookery. The first few seals came in 1990.
